source.title: Unlocking High-Accuracy Differentially Private Image Classification through Scale
source.authors: Soham De; Leonard Berrada; Jamie Hayes; Samuel L. Smith; Borja Balle

record.tranche_reason: Tests randomly initialized image classifiers trained with DP-SGD, extending the training-error question to private training; its own training-accuracy results do not reach near-zero error.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports training accuracy for the ablation pipeline. Figure 2 and Figure 3 describe training-accuracy improvements, but provide figure-only values. Test-accuracy results do not measure the training-error claim; cited results from other papers are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures training classification accuracy of randomly initialized convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 under DP-SGD. This tests an extension of V1 to private training, where clipping, added noise and privacy-limited training budgets materially change the optimization setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the conclusion: scaling models, compute and public pre-training data, together with training modifications, substantially reduces the accuracy gap between private and non-private image classification. The authors do not claim near-zero training error; their principal conclusion concerns predictive accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DP-SGD with per-example gradient clipping and added Gaussian noise, plus tuned privacy budgets and other training modifications; the claim concerns ordinary gradient-based training and near-zero training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy changes with group normalization, batch size, weight standardization, augmentation multiplicity, and exponential moving average; batch size and augmentation multiplicity also affect the reported training-accuracy trend.

fits_no_version.finding: Group normalization and weight standardization improve final training accuracy under DP-SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alternatives to batch normalization can improve private optimization; this does not measure V6's batch-normalization speed or learning-rate comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix B.2 reports slower initial convergence and degraded training performance for deeper residual networks, with depth benefits depending on privacy budget and augmentation multiplicity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The useful depth of privately trained residual networks depends on training budget and augmentation; this does not establish V3's plain-network versus shortcut comparison.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 ablation reports training accuracy on a 45K training split under DP-SGD, not ordinary non-private SGD or Adam. The ImageNet random-initialization experiment used a single random seed and a limited hyperparameter sweep. Figure 2 and Figure 3 provide trends without extractable exact values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Test accuracies and validation-only depth results were excluded because they do not measure training classification error.

untested.parts: Near-zero error under ordinary non-private SGD or Adam; corrupted or random labels; CIFAR-100 training error; sufficiently large model-size sweeps demonstrating interpolation.
ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons between plain batch-normalized networks and networks with identity shortcuts; the specified tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons in plain networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and trainable depth.
Initial linearized stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature trajectories and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable Fixup training.

missing.what: Training accuracy has an interior optimum as noise and the privacy-permitted iteration budget increase. For WRN-16-4, the optimum is approximately sigma=3 and 2500 iterations; longer permitted training with greater noise reduces training accuracy. WRN-40-4 shows the same qualitative behavior. Add training-accuracy rows, retaining figure-value uncertainty.
missing.locator: Section 5, Figure 6(c); Appendix B.5, Figure 10 training-accuracy panel

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. Final accuracy improvements do not establish faster training, and group normalization is not batch normalization. Missing numerical figure values are an evidence limitation, not independently a scope-limiting result.

versions.untested_parts: Corrupted or random labels, non-private SGD or Adam, CIFAR-100 from random initialization, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
